preamble: The change of the labio-velar approximant [w] to the bilabial nasal [m] happens when [w] stands before a nasal vowel: the velum lowering of the vowel spreads onto the glide, and a nasalized labial closure is heard as [m]. Mandan has this as a synchronic rule (/w/ > [m] before nasal vowels). Historically it shows up in Iroquoian, where Proto-Iroquoian *awẽʔ 'water' gave Cherokee ama and Laurentian ame, and in Mixtec varieties, where Proto-Mixtec *w became m before nasalized vowels.

examples.note: Synchronic rule: /w/ and /r/ are realized as [m] and [n] before nasal vowels.
*w became m before the nasalized vowel, which then lost its nasality.
Contrast the other Northern Iroquoian reflexes, which keep w: Tuscarora à·węʔ, Mohawk awe’-, Wyandot awen’.

examples.to: Alcozauca kaꞌmi; San Juan Colorado cahmi
